title: Strategic correction: prioritize algorithm discovery over lower-bound research
question: How should capacity be allocated to maximize the chance of a working faster ECDLP algorithm?
rationale: User directive (2026-11-03): the lab drifted toward proving barriers; the primary mission is a universal classical algorithm beating generic square-root complexity. Supersedes the round-10 allocation DEC. Existing results and formal proofs are retained.
claims: Allocation: 60% constructive algorithm discovery and implementation (algorithm-inventor role), 20% experimental falsification and scaling benchmarks vs Pollard rho, 10% directly relevant mathematical proofs, 10% literature review and publication.

Every algorithmic candidate must give: mechanism revealing information about k; pseudocode and prototype; correctness argument; explicit complexity model incl. preprocessing and memory; measured scaling vs Pollard rho; exact obstacle if unsuccessful.
No further interpolation lower-bound variants unless they unblock an active algorithmic candidate. Running ECDLP-38 (conjecture C*) is allowed to finish but receives no follow-up.
Success criterion: a working faster algorithm — not the number of theorems, PRs or papers. No speedup is claimed without measured evidence; no positive results are manufactured.
notes: Recorded by PI RUN-62dbda7c on user instruction.
